text: P1: the model prefers the indirect object over the repeated subject (accuracy > 0.8, logit difference > 0).
the IOI dataset on this tokenizer
E0002 (full precision (local)): accuracy 0.91, logit difference 3.81 on 32 prompts.
logit lens: where does the answer become readable at END?
E0003: the logit difference read off the residual stream reaches half its final value at layer 8 of 11.

P2 (hand-off): with a corruption that only changes which name is repeated, patching the clean residual stream at S2 restores the behaviour in early layers but not in late ones, and patching at END does the opposite. Against: no layer where S2 restores more than half, or END never takes over.
P2: residual patching at S2 and END, flip corruption
E0004 (full precision (local)): S2 patching restores up to 1.00 (early) and 0.00 at the last layer; END patching goes from -0.00 to 0.97. END overtakes S2 at layer 9 of 11.

P3 (name movers): the answer is written at END by attention in a few late layers, and within those layers by a few heads: patching the three strongest heads from the clean run restores at least 30% of the logit difference. Against: the effect is spread evenly over heads, or sits in MLPs only.
P3: all attention heads of a layer at END, by layer
P3: heads of layer 9 at END
P3: heads of layer 7 at END
E0005, E0006, E0007 (full precision (local)): attention at END matters most in layers [9, 7] (effects 1.25, 0.08). Strongest heads: 9.9 (0.85), 9.6 (0.29), 7.9 (0.05); together 1.19.

P4 (backup): mean-ablating the three strongest heads together removes clearly less of the logit difference than their patching effect, because other heads compensate. Against: the drop is as large as the patching effect.
P4: joint mean-ablation of ['9.9', '9.6', '7.9'] at END
E0008 (full precision (local)): with ['9.9', '9.6', '7.9'] mean-ablated, 0.85 of the logit difference is left (drop 0.15); patching the same heads restored 1.19.
